answer: Dune-Anchored State Divergence. Each identity writes its full interaction history to a shared append-only ledger, and a duplicated identity's two branches soon report conflicting states at the same sequence number. Any peer can diff them and flag the fork. To avoid detection, an attacker must sustain two fully isolated, continuously reconciled histories across every counter it operates, paying bandwidth and compute for each clone it spawns. A violet tag marks unresolved forks, and ivory badges are issued only after a clean audit.
